summary: This work presents a traceable in situ microwave power measurement method for superconducting quantum circuits in dilution refrigerators using AC/DC thermal substitution with a custom variable temperature stage (VTS). The method combines cryogenic calorimetry with SOLR scattering-parameter calibration to measure incident RF power at the device reference plane, demonstrating measurements from $-43$ to $-58$ dBm with relative uncertainties ranging from 2% to 40%.
motivation: Accurate knowledge of microwave power delivered to cryogenic quantum devices is essential for precise circuit-QED characterization and device operation, yet this is difficult to obtain inside dilution refrigerators due to distributed cable attenuation, temperature-dependent component behavior, and impedance mismatches between room temperature and the millikelvin stage.
method: A macroscopic OFHC copper VTS thermally weakly coupled to the dilution refrigerator's cold finger ($\sim 80$ mK) is alternately heated by DC (four-wire resistor) and RF (20 dB pass-through attenuator) while measuring temperature transients via RuOx thermometry. Steady-state temperatures are fit with a thermal model to perform AC/DC power substitution, then corrected via cryogenic SOLR calibration of the attenuator's scattering parameters ($|S_{11}|$, $|S_{21}|$) to refer the result to the DUT plane.
result: RF power measurements between $-43.87$ dBm (40.9 nW, 2% uncertainty) and $-57.58$ dBm (1.74 nW, 40% uncertainty) at 4 GHz, with dominant uncertainty contributions from parasitic heating fluctuations ($P_0$) and VTS steady-state temperature extraction; lower-power sensitivity is limited by signal indistinguishability from the $\sim 91$ nW background power.
